$comment: Every CI job, what it checks, how to reproduce and fix it, what evidence it leaves, and what each rule its tools report beyond .github/bot/rules means (ADR-0019, decisions 5 and 7). A job of a called workflow is named <caller>/<job>. tests/Arch/TheGatesAreExplainedTest.php holds this file to the workflows.

scope.checks: Which of the PHP gates a change needs: a change to documentation alone needs none.
scope.why: It decides which gates run and checks nothing itself.

attribution.checks: No commit, and not the pull request's body, credits an AI assistant or a tool.

rules.attribution: The check could not read the commits.
rules.credits-an-assistant: A commit or the pull request's body carries a co-author trailer or a badge that credits an assistant or a tool. The work is the author's own: remove the line, and reword the commit if it is in one.

commitlint.checks: Every commit subject, and the pull request title, is conventional: type(scope): subject.
commitlint.reproduce: python3 .github/scripts/commit_lint.py origin/main HEAD --title "<the pull request title>"

rules.commitlint: The check could not read the commits.
rules.conventional-subject: A commit subject is not conventional. Reword it as type(scope): subject, with a type from feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore, ci, perf, build, style or revert.
rules.conventional-title: The pull request title is not conventional. A squash merge makes it the subject of the commit on main, so write it as type(scope): subject.

description.checks: The pull request's body: every Spec: line names a decision in .docs/decisions, and a breaking title (feat!:) has a Migration section.
description.reproduce: PR_TITLE="<the title>" PR_BODY="<the body>" python3 .github/scripts/pr_text.py origin/main HEAD

rules.description: The check could not read the pull request's changes.
rules.unknown-spec: A Spec: line names a number that is no decision in .docs/decisions. The body becomes main's commit message, so it names only decisions that exist.
rules.missing-migration: The title marks a breaking change, and the body has no Migration section saying what a user changes. Add a ## Migration section.
rules.suggest-title: A conventional title for these changes starts like this.
rules.suggest-spec: These changes touch paths that belong to these decisions. Name the one this pull request follows with a Spec: line.

pr-evidence.checks: It gathers the pr workflow's evidence into the one artifact the bot reads.
pr-evidence.why: It holds the other jobs' evidence and checks nothing itself.

scripts.checks: The deciding half of every script under .github/scripts, by its unit tests.

rules.scripts: The tests did not run to the end.
rules.error: A test threw before it could finish.

rules.checks: The architecture rules of ARCHITECTURE.md: layers, shapes, names and the tests themselves (tests/Arch).

rules.pest: The suite did not run to the end, so it wrote no log of its tests.
rules.error: A test threw before it could finish.

guards.checks: Every rule refuses a violation of itself, planted in a copy of the checkout.

rules.pest: The suite did not run to the end, so it wrote no log of its tests.
rules.failure: A rule let a planted violation of itself through.
rules.error: A test threw before it could finish.

checks.checks: The manifest, the formatting (Pint), the static analysis (PHPStan), dead idioms (Rector), the advisories and the dependencies.
checks.reproduce: composer validate --strict && composer normalize --dry-run && composer audit --locked && composer lint && composer analyse && composer refactor && composer deps
checks.fix: composer refactor:fix && composer lint:fix && composer normalize

rules.composer-validate: composer.json is not valid. Run composer validate --strict for what it says.
rules.composer-normalize: composer.json is not normalized. composer normalize writes it in the order and shape it wants.
rules.composer-audit: The audit did not run to the end.
rules.advisory: A package the lock file installs has a security advisory. Raise it to a release the advisory says is fixed.
rules.abandoned: A package the lock file installs is abandoned. Replace it with the package its author names, or drop it.
rules.pint: Pint did not run to the end.
rules.phpstan: PHPStan did not run to the end, or failed outside any file.
rules.rector: Rector did not run to the end.
rules.dependency-analyser: The dependency analyser did not run to the end.
rules.unknown-classes: The code uses a class that no installed package declares.
rules.unknown-functions: The code calls a function that no installed package declares.
rules.shadow-dependencies: The code uses a package that composer.json does not require; it arrives only through another package. Require it.
rules.dev-dependencies-in-production-code: Code under src uses a package that composer.json requires only for development.
rules.prod-dependencies-used-only-in-dev-paths: A package required for production is used only by the tests. Move it to require-dev.
rules.unused-dependencies: composer.json requires a package that nothing uses. Remove it.
rules.unused-ignore: composer-dependency-analyser.php ignores a problem that no longer occurs. Remove the ignore.

tests.checks: The suite, with every line of src covered (G7).

rules.pest: The suite did not run to the end, so it wrote no log of its tests.
rules.error: A test threw before it could finish.
rules.coverage: The suite did not run to the end, so it wrote no coverage report.
rules.uncovered: No test runs this line. Every line of src is covered: add the test that runs it, or remove the line.

lowest.checks: The suite against the oldest release of every dependency composer.json admits.

rules.pest: The suite did not run to the end, so it wrote no log of its tests.
rules.failure: A test's expectation failed against the lowest dependencies: a lower bound in composer.json no longer works.
rules.error: A test threw against the lowest dependencies: a lower bound in composer.json no longer works.

runner-contracts.checks: ADR-0004's Runner contract suite against the real Pest and Infection, at both ends of the ranges the package supports.
runner-contracts.reproduce: vendor/bin/pest --testsuite=Contract, after installing the fixture libraries as the job does

rules.pest: The suite did not run to the end, so it wrote no log of its tests.
rules.failure: A runner broke a promise of the Runner port.
rules.error: A contract test threw before it could finish.

sonar.checks: SonarCloud's analysis of the reports tests and coverage wrote.
sonar.reproduce: Open the SonarCloud project from the job's summary
sonar.why: SonarCloud reports on its own pages, and the gate job counts what it found.

gate.checks: Zero SonarCloud issues: none new on the pull request, and none open against main.

rules.sonar: The gate could not read SonarCloud's counts: the tests or the scan did not pass, or SonarCloud did not answer.
rules.sonar-new-issues: SonarCloud finds issues this pull request brings. Fix each, or resolve it in SonarCloud with the reason it is not a defect.
rules.sonar-open-issues: SonarCloud finds issues open against main. This repository allows none.

evidence.checks: It gathers every job's evidence into the one artifact the bot reads.
evidence.why: It holds the other jobs' evidence and checks nothing itself.

hygiene/actionlint.checks: The workflows, by actionlint and the shellcheck it runs over their scripts.

rules.actionlint: actionlint did not run to the end.
rules.syntax-check: A workflow is not valid YAML, or not a shape GitHub Actions reads.
rules.expression: A ${{ }} expression is wrong, or puts untrusted input straight into a script.
rules.action: A step uses an action with inputs it does not have, or misses one it needs.
rules.events: A workflow's trigger is not an event GitHub raises, or is written wrongly.
rules.workflow-call: A reusable workflow is called with inputs or secrets it does not declare.
rules.shellcheck: shellcheck finds a problem in a run: script.
rules.pyflakes: pyflakes finds a problem in a Python run: script.
rules.id: A job or step id is not valid, or not unique.
rules.shell-name: A step names a shell GitHub Actions does not have.
rules.runner-label: A job asks for a runner label that does not exist.
rules.permissions: A permissions block names a scope or a level that does not exist.
rules.if-cond: An if: condition is always true or always false as written.
rules.glob: A glob in a filter is not valid.
rules.credentials: A workflow writes a password into a container's credentials.
rules.matrix: A matrix is written wrongly, or holds a duplicate.
rules.job-needs: A job needs a job that does not exist, or the needs form a loop.
rules.deprecated-commands: A step uses a workflow command GitHub has retired.
rules.env-var: An environment variable's name is not valid.
rules.config: actionlint's own configuration is not valid.

hygiene/zizmor.checks: The workflows and dependabot.yml, audited by zizmor for the ways a workflow is attacked.

rules.zizmor: zizmor did not run to the end.
rules.adhoc-packages: A step installs a package outside a lock file, so what it installs can change between runs.
rules.anonymous-definition: A workflow or action has no name.
rules.archived-uses: A step uses an action whose repository is archived, so it gets no more fixes.
rules.artipacked: A checkout keeps its token in .git, where a later step or an uploaded artifact can reach it. Set persist-credentials: false.
rules.bot-conditions: A condition trusts an actor's name to mean a bot, which a person can spoof.
rules.cache-poisoning: A release workflow restores a cache that a less trusted run could have written.
rules.concurrency-limits: A workflow sets no concurrency, so runs of it pile up.
rules.dangerous-triggers: A workflow runs on an event, such as pull_request_target or workflow_run, that gives a pull request's content a token that can write.
rules.dependabot-cooldown: An ecosystem in dependabot.yml offers a release before it has waited seven days.
rules.dependabot-execution: dependabot.yml lets Dependabot run code from outside the repository.
rules.excessive-permissions: A workflow or job holds more permissions than it uses. Give each job only what it writes, under permissions: {}.
rules.forbidden-uses: A step uses an action this repository's configuration forbids.
rules.github-app: A GitHub App token is minted with more reach than the job needs.
rules.github-env: A step writes to GITHUB_ENV or GITHUB_PATH from a context an attacker can influence.
rules.hardcoded-container-credentials: A container's registry password is written into the workflow.
rules.impostor-commit: An action is pinned to a commit that is not in its repository, only in a fork of it.
rules.insecure-commands: A workflow turns the deprecated set-env and add-path commands back on.
rules.insecure-url-scheme: A URL uses a scheme without TLS, such as http://.
rules.known-vulnerable-actions: A step uses an action release with a published vulnerability. Move it to a fixed release.
rules.misfeature: A workflow uses a GitHub Actions feature that is unsafe by design.
rules.obfuscation: An expression or uses: is written in a roundabout form that hides what it does.
rules.overprovisioned-secrets: A job reads the whole secrets context where it needs one secret.
rules.ref-confusion: An action is pinned to a name that is both a branch and a tag.
rules.ref-version-mismatch: The version comment on a SHA-pinned action is not the tag that SHA is.
rules.secrets-inherit: A reusable workflow is called with secrets: inherit, which hands it every secret.
rules.secrets-outside-env: A job reads a secret without a GitHub environment guarding it.
rules.self-hosted-runner: A job runs on a self-hosted runner, which a pull request's code can persist on.
rules.self-repository: An in-repository action or workflow is called as ./..., which loads whatever the workspace holds at run time; GitHub's $/... form does not.
rules.stale-action-refs: An action is pinned to a SHA that no tag of it points at.
rules.superfluous-actions: A step uses an action for what the runner image already does.
rules.template-injection: A ${{ }} expression puts text from the event into a script. Pass it through env: and read the variable.
rules.typosquat-uses: A step uses an action whose name imitates a well-known one.
rules.undocumented-permissions: A permission is granted without a comment saying what it is for.
rules.unpinned-images: A container image is not pinned by digest.
rules.unpinned-tools: A tool is installed without a pinned version.
rules.unpinned-uses: An action is used by a tag or a branch, not by a commit SHA.
rules.unredacted-secrets: A secret is used in a way that GitHub's log masking does not cover.
rules.unsound-condition: An if: is always true because of how it is written, such as text around a ${{ }}.
rules.unsound-contains: contains() is called on text where a list was meant, so a substring passes.
rules.unsound-ternary: An a && b || c expression gives c when b is empty or false.
rules.use-trusted-publishing: A release publishes with a long-lived token where trusted publishing works.

hygiene/typos.checks: The spelling of every file, by typos.

rules.typos: typos did not run to the end.
rules.typo: A word typos knows as a misspelling. Its correction is proposed, not applied: inside an identifier, the corrected word can be wrong.

hygiene/links.checks: Every link in the Markdown, by lychee.

rules.lychee: lychee did not run to the end, or found no link where there are some.
rules.broken-link: A link answers 404 or 410, points at a file that is not there, or timed out.

rules.markdownlint: markdownlint did not run to the end.
rules.markdownlint-table: .github/bot/rules/markdownlint.json is not what the locked markdownlint says of its rules. Run node .github/bot/markdownlint/rules.mjs > .github/bot/rules/markdownlint.json and commit it.

security/gitleaks.checks: No secret anywhere in the history, by gitleaks.

rules.gitleaks: gitleaks did not run to the end.
rules.gitleaks-freshness: The pinned gitleaks is more than 30 days behind its latest release, so it misses rules the latest has. Raise GITLEAKS_VERSION and GITLEAKS_SHA256 in .github/workflows/security.yml.
rules.secret: gitleaks finds a secret committed here. Revoke it first, then remove it from the history; deleting the file in a later commit leaves it readable.

security/osv-scanner.checks: No known vulnerability in what the lock files install, by osv-scanner.

rules.osv-scanner: osv-scanner did not run to the end.
rules.vulnerability: A package a lock file installs has a known vulnerability. Raise it to a release the advisory says is fixed.
